LOSSES: EXPERIMENT, NORMALIZATION AND CREDIT MIX
G5-G6 | Reckoning -> focused compounding -> reacceleration
|
|-- Reported transaction and loan losses
|   |-- [R] FY22 $134.929M; FY23 $152M; FY24 $227M; FY25 $417M
|   |-- [R] FY25 loss / GPV = 417 / 248,100 x 10,000 = 16.8bp
|   `-- [I] Multi-product numerator: this is not a Payments loss rate.
|
|-- Capital provisions inside the broader cost layer
|   |-- [R] FY25 loans $153M + cash advances $32M = $185M
|   |-- [R] $185M / $417M = 44.4% of total transaction and loan losses
|   `-- [I] Provision share does not measure realized cohort default rates.
|
|-- G5 Q3 2025 onboarding experiment / adaptation
|   |-- [R] Seed: total losses 5.2% of revenue
|   |-- [S] Call rounds to 5%; mostly Payments onboarding experiments.
|   |-- [S] Changes already lowering payment loss rates
|   `-- [S] Capital volume and a slight loss-rate rise also contributed.
|
|-- Q4 normalization claim: keep its time boundary
|   |-- [S] Q4 2025 total losses returned to approximately 3% of revenue.
|   |-- [S] Q1 2026: 3.7%; Credit largest driver of year-on-year increase
|   |-- [S] Q1 Payments loss rate below prior-year Q1
|   |-- [S] Q2 2026: 3.9%; Capital a larger driver
|   `-- [S] Q2 Payments and Credit loss rates described as normalized.
|
`-- [X] A durable return of total losses to about 3% is contradicted.
    Payments loss normalization -[D:untestable]-> total-loss normalization
    Q1/Q2 2026 total-loss figures -[D:contra]-> durable 3% claim
